annihilation.short: A positron and an electron convert into, most often, two photons of about 511 keV each.

attenuation.short: Loss of photons from a line of response by absorption or scattering in the body.

ctr.short: Coincidence timing resolution: the FWHM of the measured arrival-time difference for true pairs.

dead-time.short: Time during which a detector or its electronics cannot record a new event.

doi.short: Depth of interaction: where along the crystal depth the photon interacted. Knowing it reduces parallax blur.

energy-window.short: The accepted range of measured photon energies, for example 435–650 keV.

fbp.short: Filtered backprojection: an analytic reconstruction that ramp-filters projections and smears them back.

fwhm.short: Full width at half maximum: the width of a peak at half its height.

half-life.short: The time for half of the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay.

list-mode.short: Storage of each coincidence as a record with its detector pair, time and often energy.

lor.short: Line of response: the line between the two detectors that recorded a coincidence.

michelogram.short: A map of detector-ring pairs showing which axial combinations are accepted and how they are grouped.

mlem.short: Maximum-likelihood expectation maximisation: an iterative reconstruction for Poisson data using all projections per update.

mu-map.short: An image of linear attenuation coefficients at 511 keV, used for attenuation correction.

necr.short: Noise-equivalent count rate, T²/(T+S+2R): a count-rate figure of merit that penalises scatter and randoms.

non-collinearity.short: The small deviation of the two annihilation photons from exactly 180°, about 0.5° FWHM.

normalisation.short: Correction for unequal efficiency between detector pairs.

osem.short: Ordered-subset EM: MLEM that updates the image with interleaved subsets of projection angles.

partial-volume.short: Loss of apparent contrast in objects that are small relative to the resolution, through spill-out and spill-in.

patlak.short: A graphical method that estimates the net influx rate Ki of an irreversibly trapped tracer.

positron-range.short: The distance a positron travels before it annihilates.

prompt-gamma.short: A gamma ray emitted together with the positron by some isotopes, such as Ga-68 and Rb-82.

psf.short: Point-spread function: the image of a point source. PSF modelling includes it in the system matrix.

radiotracer.short: A biologically active molecule labelled with a radioactive isotope.

randoms.short: Accidental coincidences between photons from two unrelated annihilations.

scatter.short: Coincidences in which at least one photon changed direction in the body before detection.

scintillator.short: A crystal that converts deposited gamma-ray energy into a pulse of visible light.

sinogram.short: A histogram of coincidences indexed by line position s and angle φ.

sipm.short: Silicon photomultiplier: a solid-state sensor that converts scintillation light into an electrical pulse.

suv.short: Standardised uptake value: tissue activity concentration divided by injected activity per body weight.

suvr.short: SUV ratio: mean uptake in a target region divided by mean uptake in a reference region.

system-matrix.short: The model A whose element Aij is the expected contribution of voxel j to measurement bin i.

tof.short: Time of flight: using the photons’ arrival-time difference to localise an event along its line of response.

trues.short: Coincidences from one annihilation whose two photons both reached the detectors unscattered.
